name: m2_split
_comment: M2 measure-first (owner decision 2026-09-30).  In ../bf-tree a 'full page' is a
copy of the base leaf in the ring: page-granular caching inside the same pool as
the records.  This fork already HAS a page-granular cache -- SQLite's pcache --
and the harness gives it part of BF's budget.  So M2's question can be asked
with no code: at a FIXED total, move memory between the record ring and the
page cache and see which granularity serves more reads per byte.
ring_bytes 2/4/8/16/32 MiB, page cache = 36 MiB - ring; stock = 36 MiB pcache
read_zipf     point reads, scrambled zipf (YCSB): hot keys spread over leaves
read_zipfraw  point reads, contiguous zipf: hot keys share leaves -- where a
scan_zipfraw  32-row range scans: the record cache does not serve scans, so
this arm isolates the page cache
If page caching wins per byte on zipfraw, M2 is worth building (as a unified
pool); if records win or it is a wash, M2 is a documented non-transfer.
Read seek hit %, cached_records, evictions and pg hit % beside ops/s.
